items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Nate Chinen who wrote my book, by putting his name on the cover and giving him the promotion that, you know, was there instead of just being ghost writer.

ctx.x: What makes your heart gladdest about opportunities that you were able to give people? Are there any that just … you just …
Well, I just mentioned about Nate Chinen who wrote my book, by putting his name on the cover and giving him the promotion that, you know, was there instead of just being ghost

writer. I helped him create a career and a life. And I've done that with a few musicians too. Some appreciate it, some didn't. Ruby Braff never appreciated it. He could have been a much bigger name, but Ruby was an anachronism. He … he's a great trumpet player but he played in a traditional style and didn't play … so the critics never …. He was a better musician, a creative player. And Ruby's last words, the last time I spoke to him was – we were talking about the old days – and he said to me, "You were all right…
